question: Is the proposed v1 recovery contract—fail closed, preserve uncertain provenance, return `update_partial`, then require status/Doctor inspection and a fresh plan—acceptable for package-installer and Gateway scheduler failures?
rationale: Tests can establish local control flow, but maintainers must decide whether the user-facing recovery burden and residual external state are acceptable for this experimental lifecycle feature.

options.title: Require live recovery proof first
options.body: Keep the fail-closed design, but require redacted live package and Gateway failure/retry evidence that shows an operator can identify and safely recover the resulting partial state before merge.

options.title: Narrow v1 scope
options.body: Defer external package and Gateway mutation from `claws update` until a stronger reconcile or operation-identity design is available, while retaining the read-only planner.

options.title: Accept the documented experimental contract
options.body: Merge with `update_partial` as the supported recovery outcome, explicitly accepting manual operator inspection for uncertain external mutations.

recommendation.title: Require live recovery proof first
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed design, but require redacted live package and Gateway failure/retry evidence that shows an operator can identify and safely recover the resulting partial state before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review comment identifies the exact unresolved user-recovery and aggregate-consent decision.
